searchText: Why is the flow broken? Is it that we now need to get the full thing and not just the transactions? I think the same semantics should be preserved, the CL will keep a blinded execution payload envelope, and will the request the entire execution Payload from the EL to assemble the envelope It's broken because you need the full execution payload and not just the transactions. Payload bodies doesn't provide the full payload At least not unless we create a new version Ah yeah with that I agree, we need to recover the full Payload. But I often wandered about the usefulness of that method itself... I'll ask that question in the call I guess My initial thoughts are we shouldn't even need to do this in the CL. The CL only serves consensus data to users, which always includes the header instead of the full payload. If users want full EL data, they could obtain it directly from the EL. The separation of concern is nice. That said, I think I missed an important point, which is that the CL needs to serve payloads by ranges over P2P I have a question regarding payload attestations rewards: are payload attestations older than the ones for the current block being considered for this first ePBS implementation? payload attestations older than current block slot - 1 are not considered, and will never be considered i've added it to the agenda anyway https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1150#issuecomment-2341455541 Why never considered? in principle it's something we could implement, without much more complexity... just thought originally that it wasn't really important, that's why we didn't I used a strong word. I just meant never, as the spec doesn't allow it, so unless we change the spec, I don’t see why we would want to allow it other than to reward honest payload attestations of `n` if the `n+1` block is missed. Anything else? yeah just to not miss rewards in case of reorgs and the such I don't think this is really important Thank you for clearing this aspect PTC just gets vanilla attestation rewards, right? No changes there in rewards PTC gets one full attestation reward. No changes there

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Why is the flow broken? Is it that we now need to get the full thing and not just the transactions? I think the same semantics should be preserved, the CL will keep a blinded execution payload envelope, and will the request the entire execution Payload from the EL to assemble the envelope

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: It's broken because you need the full execution payload and not just the transactions. Payload bodies doesn't provide the full payload

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: At least not unless we create a new version

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Ah yeah with that I agree, we need to recover the full Payload. But I often wandered about the usefulness of that method itself... I'll ask that question in the call I guess

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: My initial thoughts are we shouldn't even need to do this in the CL. The CL only serves consensus data to users, which always includes the header instead of the full payload. If users want full EL data, they could obtain it directly from the EL. The separation of concern is nice. That said, I think I missed an important point, which is that the CL needs to serve payloads by ranges over P2P

excerpts.author: kboom_ro
excerpts.content: I have a question regarding payload attestations rewards: are payload attestations older than the ones for the current block being considered for this first ePBS implementation?

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: payload attestations older than current block slot - 1 are not considered, and will never be considered

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content:
i've added it to the agenda anyway
https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1150#issuecomment-2341455541

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Why never considered? in principle it's something we could implement, without much more complexity... just thought originally that it wasn't really important, that's why we didn't

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I used a strong word. I just meant never, as the spec doesn't allow it, so unless we change the spec, I don’t see why we would want to allow it other than to reward honest payload attestations of `n` if the `n+1` block is missed. Anything else?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah just to not miss rewards in case of reorgs and the such

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I don't think this is really important
